newsitem.title: USA: Prime Hospitality to buy Homegate for $132 million.
newsitem.headline: Prime Hospitality to buy Homegate for $132 million.

text.p: Prime Hospitality Corp. said Friday it would buy Homegate Hospitality Inc., another hotel holding company, for about $132 million in stock.
The combined company will operate about 150 hotels by year-end, with about 70 more AmeriSuites and Homegate properties under development.

Under the definitive agreement, Prime will issue 0.6073 share of its common stock for each of the about 10.7 million outstanding Homegate shares. It said it valued the deal at about $132 million based on Prime's closing stock price of $20.375 on Thursday.
Prime's shares fell $1.56 to $18.81 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday. Homegate rose $1.06 to $10.56 on Nasdaq after being halted for trading earlier.
Prime currently owns or operates 112 hotels, while Homegate owns eight hotels and is developing another 34.

"Homegate is an excellent complement to our AmeriSuites and Wellesley Inns brands," Prime Chief Executive David Simon said in a statement. "The Homegate hotels generate excellent investment returns, comparable to our AmeriSuites."
Simon said he expected the merger to contribute to Fairfield, N.J.-based Prime's earnings in 1998.
Prime said it would provide $65 million in financing to Homegate after the merger closes to facilitate uninterrupted development of Homegate's extended-stay hotels.

It will manage the Homegate hotels after the merger and will pay $12 million to Wyndham Hotel Corp. to end current management agreements. Prime said it will pay Wyndham $8 million and one of Homegate's founding stockholders will chip in $4 million.
Prime said it expected the deal to close in the fourth quarter, subject to the approval of Homegate shareholders.

Homegate, based in Austin, Texas, said its shareholders holding about 59 percent of the company's outstanding shares, including affiliates of Crow Investment Trust and Greystar Capital Partners, agreed to vote in favour of the transaction.
Homegate posted a loss of $866,000 on revenues of $2.7 million in its first year of operation from Feb. 9 through Dec. 31, 1996.

Prime announced on Wednesday that it hired Montgomery Securities to advise it on a possible sale and leaseback arrangement for nine full-service hotels. Prime said it plans to use the proceeds to develop hotels, including AmeriSuites and Homegates.
